sheet-1.description: This part is the lower half of Sheet 1, below the heavy line that separates it from the key map, street index and title cartouche at the top of the sheet. Drawn at 100 feet to an inch, it covers the southwestern edge of Manville between Roosevelt Avenue and the Royce Branch, a subdivision that was almost entirely laid out but scarcely built on in 1928. Roosevelt Avenue runs across the top of the part, with the ends of Arizona, Carolina, Connecticut and Delaware Avenues coming down to it from the north. South of Roosevelt Avenue the plan is irregular: Arkansas and California Avenues run south, Colorado Avenue curves through the middle of the tract and turns south near Jackson, and Wilson Avenue and Riverside Avenue follow the bend of the Royce Branch, which runs along the bottom of the part. Adams and Jackson are short streets between them, and Acton Court, marked arbitrary, is a lane near the brook. The blocks, numbered 128 to 139, are cut into many narrow house lots, some fan-shaped along the curves, with only about twenty small frame dwellings and outbuildings scattered among them, mostly along Roosevelt Avenue and the upper part of Colorado Avenue. The west edge is marked no exposure, and block 127 beyond Arkansas Avenue is left blank. A large compass rose with a magnetic needle stands at the left, and the 100 foot scale bar is printed at the lower right.
notes: The upper half of the sheet (key map at 900 feet to an inch, index and title) is outside this part's mask and is not georeferenced.

Modern names at Roosevelt Avenue: Arizona Avenue = South 20th Avenue, Carolina = South 17th, Connecticut = South 15th, Delaware = South 14th; Colorado Avenue meets Roosevelt Avenue at South 16th Avenue, as the modern Colorado Avenue does.
Wilson, Riverside, Adams, Jackson and Acton Court do not exist today; the modern Colorado Avenue and Coolidge Avenue follow parts of the drawn plan and gave two control points off Roosevelt Avenue.

Map, 100 ft. Top half is the key map (900 ft), index and title: outside the mask. Lower half: Roosevelt Av to Royce Branch (Arizona/Carolina/Connecticut/Delaware = S 20th/17th/15th/14th Av; Colorado Av meets Roosevelt at S 16th). One part.

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the compact commercial and industrial core of Manville around the Lehigh Valley Railroad and Millstone Road, and is drawn at 50 feet to an inch, unlike the 100 foot sheets around it. The wide band of the L. V. R. R. tracks crosses the sheet diagonally from lower left to upper right. North of the tracks lies a rail-served industrial tract bounded by Brooks Boulevard: a shirt factory (Mfr. of Men's Shirts) with steam, lights and power, the large Wm. Greaseheimer Lumber Yard with several lumber sheds, cement store and office, wood working shop and pump house, and the passenger station beside the tracks. At the upper left, long narrow house lots of blocks 64 and 65 lie on Wyoming Place and Maine Avenue. South of the tracks, Texas Avenue carries a row of small shops and sheds including the Manville Supply Co. (feed, coal and wood), a coal hopper and a siding that curves off the main line. Below it, Dakota Avenue and Washington Avenue bound two long blocks of mostly frame dwellings with outbuildings, a few brick and concrete block buildings, and an auto repairing shop with a concrete floor. Pennsylvania Avenue runs down the left side. Millstone Road is the wide diagonal road on the right, shown with both edges; the 55 foot width is lettered along it. The brick and frame buildings near it include several stores. The sheet has the compass rose at the right, the Manville stamp at the upper right and a scale of feet at the bottom. The margins are left blank where the adjoining sheets 3, 5 and 10 continue the map.
notes: Drawn at 50 feet to an inch (scale bar on the sheet), not 100 feet; the pipeline config sets scale_ft 50.
Pennsylvania Avenue is South 3rd Avenue today (the fit places it there; the atlas lead's table gave 4th).
Texas Avenue is now South Street, Maine Avenue is North Street, Dakota Avenue is Dakota Street, and Millstone Road is South Main Street (North Main Street north of North Street).
Wyoming Avenue is North 4th Avenue; the avenues lettered 3rd, 2nd and 1st at the top are North 3rd, North 2nd and North 1st Avenues; Harcar Avenue is South 2nd Avenue.
Map, 50 ft. Texas (South St), Dakota, Washington Avs between Pennsylvania (S 3rd) and Millstone Rd (Main St); railroad and lumber yard north. One part (helper).

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 shows the older business and residential centre of Manville around the junction of Camplain Avenue and Millstone Road, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Washington Avenue runs along the top edge, and the north-south avenues Nebraska, Ohio, Pennsylvania and Harcar cross the upper half to Camplain Avenue, which runs left to right across the middle and bends at its junction with Millstone Road. The upper blocks hold small frame dwellings and sheds, a Baptist church, a dance hall, a bakery, a drug store and bank near Millstone Road, the Church and School of Sacred Heart (Polish) with its stone rectory and convent, and on Ohio Avenue a shirt factory and a concrete block truck garage with a capacity of ten trucks. South of Camplain Avenue the map changes orientation: Pope Street and Millstone Road run diagonally to the lower left and lower right, carrying a continuous row of two and three story brick and frame stores, the Manville Theatre (motion pictures), St. Mary's Catholic Church (Greek) with its school, and several churches and halls. At lower right Public School No. 1 stands in the block between Millstone Road, 1st Street and Gladys Avenue, and 2nd Street is at the right edge. Short, Beekman and Rosalie streets and Gladys Avenue appear at the bottom. Block numbers 95 to 99 and 118 to 121 identify the blocks, and the compass rose and Manville stamp are at the right. Sheets 5, 2, 7, 9 and 10 adjoin.
notes: Drawn at 50 feet to an inch (scale bar on the sheet); the pipeline config sets scale_ft 50.
Pennsylvania, Ohio and Nebraska Avenues are South 3rd, South 4th and South 5th Avenues (fit against Washington Avenue and Camplain Road junctions); Harcar Avenue is South 2nd Avenue.

Camplain Avenue is West Camplain Road west of Millstone Road and East Camplain Road east of it; Millstone Road is South Main Street; Filak is Filak Avenue; Short Street appears to be William Street today (not certain).
Public School No. 1 and the Church and School of Sacred Heart (Polish) are the largest institutions drawn.

Map, 50 ft. Washington Av to Rosalie, Ohio (S 4th), Pennsylvania (S 3rd), Harcar (S 2nd), Nebraska (S 5th), Camplain Av, Pope St, Millstone Rd; Public School No. 1, Sacred Heart church. One part (helper).

sheet-4-1.description: The main part of Sheet 4 covers the northwestern district of Manville between Maine Avenue, beside the Lehigh Valley Railroad tracks at the bottom of the sheet, and the subdivision north of Brooks Boulevard, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. In the lower third the state-named avenues, Florida, Georgia, Indiana, Jersey, Kentucky, Louisiana, Rhode Island, Tennessee and Utah Avenues, run up from Maine Avenue to Brooks Boulevard in long narrow blocks of house lots with scattered frame dwellings and a dairy products building. North of Brooks Boulevard the grid turns about thirty degrees: Jersey, Kentucky, Louisiana and Rhode Island Avenues continue northeastward, crossed by Herbert, Henry and Ester and with 6th Place, 6th Avenue, 5th Avenue and Louis Street at the edges, laid out in deep narrow lots, many still vacant, with small dwellings concentrated along Kentucky and Rhode Island Avenues. A heavy line along the west and north sides of this district separates it from the inset of the Pillar of Fire grounds at Zarephath, and the edge facing it is marked no exposure. A meeting hall stands outside the line at the lower left, near the end of Brooks Boulevard. The upper right corner around blocks 24 to 29 continues onto Sheet 5. A compass rose stands at the upper right and the scale bar at the bottom right.
notes: South of Brooks Boulevard the avenues are today's North 13th (Florida) to North 5th (Utah) Avenues; Maine Avenue is North Street.
North of Brooks Boulevard, Henry is today's Louis Street; Jersey, Kentucky, Louisiana and Rhode Island Avenues continue as North 10th to North 7th Avenues.
Brooks Boulevard west of Indiana Avenue is drawn with its south edge only; its junctions with Florida and Georgia Avenues were left out of the fit.
Brooks Boulevard / North 11th Avenue and Knopf Street / North 9th Avenue were 13 m off the fit and were rejected.

Map, 100 ft. Two parts: 1 main (Brooks Blvd grid N 13th-N 5th and the turned subdivision north of it; Henry = Louis St); 2 inset top left: Pillar of Fire School and Book Bindery at Zarephath (anchored on Weston Canal Road at the canal bridge, low confidence).

sheet-4-2.description: This inset in the upper left corner of Sheet 4, separated from the Manville street grid by a heavy line, shows the Pillar of Fire School and Book Bindery at Zarephath, on the far side of the Delaware and Raritan Canal from Manville. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with its own north arrow, and is turned so that north lies to the upper right. Canal Road to Bound Brook runs along the bottom of the inset beside the canal, and a road crosses the canal on a bridge and climbs in two branches to the institution's buildings. These include dormitories, a dining hall with offices and dormitory, a chapel with laboratories and further dormitories, an iron frame water tank of 50,000 gallons, and a printing, carpenter shop, Zarephath post office and store building where the book binding was done. A truck garage and auto repair shop and terra cotta tile buildings stand to the left. Two-inch and three-inch water pipes, hydrants and an observatory are marked, and a long note gives the fire protection: steam heat, electric light and power, hydrants with 750 feet of hose, extinguishers, two wells pumping into the tank, and a volunteer fire company of 25 men. The remaining area of the inset is open ground.
notes: Canal Road to Bound Brook is today's Weston Canal Road; the road over the canal bridge is today's Chapel Drive.

Placed from one hand-picked point (Weston Canal Road at the canal bridge) with the atlas scale and a rotation of 37 degrees fitted by eye to the canal and the bridge road; the inset's own north arrow points about 70 degrees clockwise from up and was not used. Low confidence.
Zarephath and the Pillar of Fire grounds lie in Franklin Township, east of the canal, about 1 km east of the Manville grid on the rest of the sheet.

Map, 100 ft. Two parts: 1 main (Brooks Blvd grid N 13th-N 5th and the turned subdivision north of it; Henry = Louis St); 2 inset top left: Pillar of Fire School and Book Bindery at Zarephath (anchored on Weston Canal Road at the canal bridge, low confidence).

sheet-5-1.description: The main part of Sheet 5 covers the north central district of Manville between Brooks Boulevard and Dukes Parkway, east of Sheet 4, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. North of Brooks Boulevard a subdivision turned about thirty degrees to the rest of the town is laid out with Louisiana, Rhode Island, 6th, 5th, 4th, 3rd, 2nd and 1st Avenues running northeast, crossed by Ester, Louis and Knopf, and bounded on the north by the curve of Dukes Parkway and on the east by Millstone Road. The blocks, numbered 19 to 265, are cut into deep narrow house lots, with small frame dwellings spread thinly along the avenues, several marked as built from plans. South of Brooks Boulevard at the right, the Hotel Asbestos with a post office stands near Millstone Road, the Lehigh Valley Railroad tracks cross the lower right corner, and a marginal note says the Johns-Manville asbestos products manufacturing plant lies beyond, admittance refused. The lower left of the sheet, west of a heavy line, and a boxed inset at the bottom centre are separate parts, and the corner above Dukes Parkway at the upper right is drawn out of place as another part. A compass rose and the scale bar are at the right edge.
notes: The numbered avenues north of Brooks Boulevard correspond to today's North 6th to North 1st Avenues; Millstone Road is today's North Main Street.
The drawn plan north of Brooks Boulevard does not match the modern streets closely: the fit has an RMSE of about 4.4 m, Louis Street junctions were 8 to 13 m off and were left out. Low confidence.
Marginal note: John Manville Asbestos Products Mfg. Plant beyond, admittance refused.

Map, 100 ft. Four parts: 1 main (turned subdivision north of Brooks Blvd, 1st-6th Avs, Knopf, Dukes Pkwy, Millstone Rd = N Main St; drawn plan fits modern streets only to about 4.4 m); 2 upper right corner, Dukes Pkwy at Millstone Rd drawn out of place (anchored); 3 strip Utah-Wyoming Avs (N 5th-3rd) between Brooks Blvd and Texas Av; 4 boxed inset blocks 82-83 (Nebraska-Pennsylvania Avs = S 5th-3rd, Texas Av to Washington Av).

sheet-5-2.description: This small part in the upper right corner of Sheet 5, cut off by a heavy line, shows the junction of Dukes Parkway with Millstone Road, drawn out of its place on the ground so that it fits on the sheet. Dukes Parkway, 50 feet wide, comes in from the left and meets Millstone Road, 55 feet wide, which runs up to the right; 1st Avenue branches off Dukes Parkway at the lower left. The only building is a large concrete-floored garage for 35 cars, with electric light and steam heat, on Millstone Road just north of the junction. Block 22 fills the rest of the part as open land, and a printed 5 marks the continuation of the sheet. The part is drawn at 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Millstone Road is today's North Main Street; Dukes Parkway keeps its name.

Placed from one hand-picked point (Dukes Parkway and North Main Street) with the atlas scale and the rotation of the measured lines; a second hand-picked point at 1st Avenue gave a scale 11 percent off and was not used. Low confidence.

Map, 100 ft. Four parts: 1 main (turned subdivision north of Brooks Blvd, 1st-6th Avs, Knopf, Dukes Pkwy, Millstone Rd = N Main St; drawn plan fits modern streets only to about 4.4 m); 2 upper right corner, Dukes Pkwy at Millstone Rd drawn out of place (anchored); 3 strip Utah-Wyoming Avs (N 5th-3rd) between Brooks Blvd and Texas Av; 4 boxed inset blocks 82-83 (Nebraska-Pennsylvania Avs = S 5th-3rd, Texas Av to Washington Av).

sheet-5-3.description: This part at the lower left of Sheet 5 covers the strip between Brooks Boulevard and the Lehigh Valley Railroad tracks from Utah Avenue to Wyoming Avenue, with a narrow band south of the tracks along Texas Avenue, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Utah, Virginia and Wyoming Avenues run down from Brooks Boulevard to Maine Avenue, which borders the railroad, and Wyoming Place leads east off Wyoming Avenue. Blocks 62 and 63 are divided into narrow house lots with a moderate number of frame dwellings, a few concrete-block buildings and outbuildings. Below the tracks, Texas Avenue runs along the bottom of the sheet with the ends of Nebraska, Ohio and Pennsylvania Avenues lettered beneath it. A heavy line on the east side separates this strip from the inset of blocks 82 and 83.
notes: Utah, Virginia and Wyoming Avenues are today's North 5th, 4th and 3rd Avenues; Wyoming Place keeps its name; Maine Avenue is North Street and Texas Avenue is South Street.
Placed from three detected junctions and one hand-picked junction (Brooks Boulevard at Virginia Avenue); the fitted scale is about 5 percent above the atlas's. Low confidence.

Map, 100 ft. Four parts: 1 main (turned subdivision north of Brooks Blvd, 1st-6th Avs, Knopf, Dukes Pkwy, Millstone Rd = N Main St; drawn plan fits modern streets only to about 4.4 m); 2 upper right corner, Dukes Pkwy at Millstone Rd drawn out of place (anchored); 3 strip Utah-Wyoming Avs (N 5th-3rd) between Brooks Blvd and Texas Av; 4 boxed inset blocks 82-83 (Nebraska-Pennsylvania Avs = S 5th-3rd, Texas Av to Washington Av).

sheet-5-4.description: This boxed inset at the bottom centre of Sheet 5 shows blocks 82 and 83, the area south of the railroad between Texas Avenue and Washington Avenue, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with its own north arrow and turned slightly to the rest of the sheet. Nebraska, Ohio and Pennsylvania Avenues run down from Texas Avenue to Washington Avenue, and Dakota Avenue leads off to the east. The blocks are cut into narrow house lots; most are vacant, with a few frame dwellings and stores near Washington Avenue, among them two buildings marked as drawn from plans and a tile partition building. Printed sheet numbers around the inset (2, 3, 5 and 7) refer to the adjoining sheets.
notes: Nebraska, Ohio and Pennsylvania Avenues are today's South 5th, 4th and 3rd Avenues; Texas Avenue is South Street; Dakota Avenue is Dakota Street.
Placed from four detected and three hand-picked junctions on Washington Avenue (RMSE 0.6 m).

Map, 100 ft. Four parts: 1 main (turned subdivision north of Brooks Blvd, 1st-6th Avs, Knopf, Dukes Pkwy, Millstone Rd = N Main St; drawn plan fits modern streets only to about 4.4 m); 2 upper right corner, Dukes Pkwy at Millstone Rd drawn out of place (anchored); 3 strip Utah-Wyoming Avs (N 5th-3rd) between Brooks Blvd and Texas Av; 4 boxed inset blocks 82-83 (Nebraska-Pennsylvania Avs = S 5th-3rd, Texas Av to Washington Av).

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 shows the western part of Manville, a regular grid of very long narrow blocks laid out for house lots, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. The Lehigh Valley Railroad crosses the sheet in a wide band of tracks from left to right a little below the upper third. North of the tracks lie blocks 46 to 53 on a platted but almost unbuilt tract between Maine Avenue and the sheet's top edge; the lots are drawn in long ranks with only a few scattered frame dwellings and outbuildings. South of the tracks Vermont Avenue runs along the railroad and the state-named avenues, Alabama, Arizona, Arkansas, California, Carolina, Colorado, Connecticut, Delaware and Florida, run north to south between blocks 67 to 74, 86 and 75. Washington Avenue crosses at the upper right, and Camplain Avenue runs across the lower part, with blocks 103 to 110 below it, ending at Roosevelt Avenue along the bottom edge. A curved stream, the continuation of the Royce Branch, closes the lower right corner. Almost all the buildings are small yellow frame dwellings and sheds on deep lots, with a handful of brick or stone buildings; many blocks are empty. The compass rose is at the lower left, the Manville stamp at the upper right, and the scale bar at the bottom right. Sheet 4 adjoins at the upper right and sheet 7 at the right.
notes: The state-named avenues are today's numbered avenues, South of the Lehigh Line and North of it: Alabama 21st, Arizona 20th, Arkansas 19th, California 18th, Carolina 17th, Colorado 16th, Connecticut 15th, Delaware 14th, Florida 13th.
Maine Avenue is North Street, Vermont Avenue is Vermont Street, Camplain Avenue is West Camplain Road.
The avenue names are lettered without an Av. suffix on the south side of the tracks (only AV. is printed on the avenues north of Maine Avenue); read at medium confidence from overview and crops.
An earlier fit with every avenue one number higher also fitted the regular grid; the numbering was corrected from sheets anchored on Main Street.
Map, 100 ft. Arizona (20th) to Florida (13th) Avs, Maine Av (North St) to Roosevelt Av; Alabama Av has no modern street. One part (helper).

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 covers the central residential grid of Manville south of the Lehigh Valley Railroad, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north turned about 17 degrees clockwise of straight up. Maine Avenue and the railroad tracks run across the top of the sheet; below them the north-south avenues named after states, Florida, Georgia, Indiana, Jersey, Kentucky, Louisiana, Mississippi, Montana and Nebraska Avenues, cross Washington Avenue and Camplain Avenue in a regular pattern of long narrow blocks divided into deep, narrow house lots numbered up to the 300s. Most buildings are small frame dwellings with outbuildings, scattered thinly across the lots, with a few stores and shops near Camplain Avenue. Institutions include St. Peters Orthodox Catholic Church, a concrete-block building on Mississippi Avenue near Washington Avenue, Manville Public School No. 2 on the block between Mississippi and Montana Avenues, and a Hungarian Church near Nebraska Avenue and Pope Street. Small industry is represented by the R. and E. Shirt Factory, a concrete-block building on Camplain Avenue west of Kentucky Avenue, another shirt factory on Louisiana Avenue, and an auto repair shop. South of Camplain Avenue, Roosevelt Avenue curves across the sheet in a broad arc, with Jefferson Avenue and Riverside Avenue laid out in a newer curving subdivision of fan-shaped lots that runs down to the Royce Branch, which crosses the bottom of the sheet. The area south of the brook is left blank apart from a block number. The upper right corner around block 81 is largely open land with a few houses. Adjoining sheets are 4 to the north, 6 to the west, 5 and 3 to the east, 1 to the southwest and 9 to the south.
notes: The state-named avenues are today's numbered avenues: Florida = 13th, Georgia = 12th, Indiana = 11th, Jersey = 10th, Kentucky = 9th, Louisiana = 8th, Mississippi = 7th, Montana = 6th, Nebraska = 5th (South south of the railroad, North north of it; Rhode Island = North 7th, Tennessee = North 6th, Utah = North 5th).
Maine Avenue is today's North Street; Camplain Avenue is today's West Camplain Road.
A first fit that put every avenue one number too high (Nebraska = South 6th) also fitted the regular grid at 0.5 m; adjoining sheets anchored on Main Street showed the one-block error.
Shows St. Peters Orthodox Catholic Church, Manville Public School No. 2, a Hungarian Church and the R. and E. Shirt Factory.

Map, 100 ft. Pilot. Central grid Florida (13th) to Nebraska (5th) Avs, Maine Av (North St) to Roosevelt Av. One part. First configured one avenue number too high; corrected after the helper's Main Street-anchored sheets showed it.

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 covers the area south of central Manville on both sides of the broad Reading Railroad (Philadelphia and Reading Railroad) right of way, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north turned about 38 degrees counterclockwise, so the streets run diagonally. West of the tracks lie Railroad Avenue, Semke Street, Frech Avenue and Engel Place, with blocks 156 and 157 of small frame dwellings, a concrete block building and a vacant building, and a wide strip of blocks 139, 158 and 154 mostly unbuilt. East of the tracks a block grid of Haran, Rabens and Fabel Avenues, crossed by Driscoll Street, Semke, King Street and Central, holds blocks 163 to 166, 191 to 195 and 207 to 208, with scattered frame dwellings on narrow lots. Trenton Avenue and Millstone Road (Stone Avenue) run diagonally across the top, with Van Neste Place and Central branching from them near block 167 and 195. At the upper right the Royce Branch, a wide stream with a pond, flows toward the right edge and is crossed by a bridge at the end of Bridge (Plank Bridge is lettered). The lower right has long diagonal blocks along Garry Street and Schmidt Street (blocks 190, 204 to 206) and Millstone Road continues to the right edge with blocks 209 to 211. The compass rose is at the left and a scale bar at the lower right. Sheets 7, 9 and 11 adjoin.
notes: Millstone Road, lettered "Millstone Rd. (Stone Av.)" on this sheet, is South Main Street today.
Central is Central Street; Frech Avenue is West Frech Avenue at its junction with Engel Place; Haran, Rabens, King, Driscoll, Garry, Schmidt, Van Neste Place and Engel Place keep their names.
Fabel Avenue, Semke, Trenton Avenue and Railroad Avenue are not in the modern street data.
Sheet is rotated: north points about 38 degrees to the left of up; fitted with 13 detected junctions, RMSE about 1.5 m.
Map, 100 ft, turned about -38 deg. South Manville: Millstone Rd (Stone Av, now S Main St), Haran, Rabens, Fabel Avs, Royce Branch. One part (helper).

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 shows the area south of the Lehigh Valley Railroad's yards on both sides of the Reading Railroad main line, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north turned about 39 degrees counterclockwise. The wide band of tracks runs from the top edge to the bottom near the middle, crossed by Park Avenue and Railroad Place at the level of block 145. West of the tracks, between Millstone Road and Gladys Avenue, small blocks 143 to 149 lie on Rosalie, Beekman, William and Short streets and Nebraska Avenue, with frame dwellings, a dance hall, a mfr. of concrete blocks and a sand pit conveyor. Nebraska Avenue, Montana Avenue and Pope Street run in from the left edge, and Riverside Avenue ends at a Royce Branch bridge. The Royce Branch curves across the lower half, with the tracks crossing it on bridges; south of it a large irregular area (blocks 142 and 144) is nearly blank apart from a farm group, an auto repairing shop and the Pennsylvania and Reading Railroad station near Railroad Avenue and Millstone Road at the bottom. East of the tracks is a separate grid of long blocks 168 to 173, 180 to 183 and 196 to 199, laid out between 6th, 5th, 4th and 3rd Avenues and Park Avenue, John Place, Fulton, Wilson Place and Woodrow, with an unnamed cross street at the top. Houses are scattered frame buildings on narrow lots. Sheets 3, 7, 8, 10 and 11 adjoin.
notes: The east grid matches today's streets as follows by the fit: 6th, 5th, 4th and 3rd Avenues are Angle, Huff, Boesel and Lincoln Avenues; Park Avenue is Kyle Street, John Place is John Place, Fulton is Benjamin Street, and the street marked Not Named is View Street.
West of the tracks, Millstone Road is South Main Street; Gladys, Rosalie, Beekman, William and Pope keep their names; Short may be William Street today.
The Millstone Road label is partly cut by the Royce Branch bridge; read at medium confidence.
Map, 100 ft, turned about -39 deg. Main St, Pope, Rosalie, east grid 3rd-6th Avs (Lincoln, Boesel, Huff, Angle), Royce Branch; area south of the brook extrapolated. One part (helper).

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 shows the eastern edge of Manville east of Millstone Road, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north nearly up. A wide diagonal band of tracks of the Reading Railroad (the Philadelphia and Reading) runs from the lower left to the upper right and divides the sheet. West of it lies the small old district: Camplain Avenue runs diagonally from Millstone Road at the left to the upper right, with blocks 121 to 124 and 150 to 153 below it laid out on a turned grid of 1st to 7th Streets, Gladys Street and Rosalie. The houses are small frame dwellings on narrow deep lots. At the upper left the Federal Creosoting Co. railroad tie creosoting plant occupies a large yard with storage tanks, retort and boiler buildings, a night watchman note and piles of railroad ties, next to the L. V. R. R. tracks. A fire department building (Fire Dept.) with its equipment list is beside Millstone Road at the left edge, where the strips of sheets 2 and 3 repeat their block numbers. East of the tracks the area is mostly open land (blocks 100, 125, 126, 174, 175 and 184) with a few scattered dwellings, 5th Avenue and 6th Avenue running along a diagonal property line, and Huff Avenue and Manville Avenue entering at the upper right. A concrete bridge carries 4th Street over the tracks. The compass rose is in the upper middle; the Manville stamp is at the top right.
notes: Camplain Avenue is East Camplain Road; Millstone Road is South Main Street; Huff and Manville Avenues keep their names; Gladys Street is Gladys Avenue.
The numbered streets crossing Gladys Street correspond (by the fit) to North Orchard, North Arlington, North Weiss and North Bridge Streets.
North is turned about 7 degrees counterclockwise; fit rests on 12 detected junctions (RMSE about 0.9 m) concentrated west of the tracks; the east part is extrapolated.
A Conc. Bridge carries 4th Street over the railroad.
Map, 100 ft, turned about -7 deg. East Camplain Rd, Gladys, numbered streets (N Orchard to N Bridge), Huff, Manville Avs; east of the tracks extrapolated. One part (helper).

sheet-11-1.description: The upper part of Sheet 11 covers the eastern end of Manville between the railroad tracks at the top left and the Millstone River, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Manville Avenue, Huff Avenue, Washington Avenue and Lincoln Avenue run across the part, crossed by 1st Street, 2nd Street and 3rd Street, forming a regular grid of long blocks, numbered 175 to 215, divided into narrow numbered house lots. At the upper left the railroad crosses diagonally beside 5th Avenue, and block 184 and part of Sheet 10 lie beyond it. Buildings are sparse: small frame dwellings and outbuildings are scattered along Manville, Huff and Lincoln Avenues, with a few more along Lincoln Avenue above the river, and most lots are still vacant. The Millstone River runs along the bottom of the part, cutting off the rear of the lots south of Lincoln Avenue, and a heavy line below it divides this part from the lower part of the sheet, which continues the same streets further east. A compass rose stands at the left edge.
notes: Washington Avenue here is today's Boesel Avenue; 2nd Street is Kosciusko Street and 3rd Street is Liberty Street.
1st Street lies about 15 m from today's Pulaski Street and was left out of the fit.

Map, 100 ft. Two parts split by a heavy line: 1 north of the Millstone River (Manville/Huff/Washington (Boesel)/Lincoln Avs, 1st-3rd Sts); 2 continuation east (3rd St = Liberty, 4th St = Cooper, Griggs Pl, diagonal Lincoln Av).

sheet-11-2.description: The lower part of Sheet 11, below the heavy line, continues the eastern end of Manville to the east of the upper part, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Manville Avenue, Huff Avenue, Washington Avenue and Lincoln Avenue run across it between 3rd Street and 4th Street, and Griggs Place runs south from Lincoln Avenue. At the right, Lincoln Avenue turns diagonally to the northeast, cutting off triangular blocks 218 and 270. The blocks, numbered 178 to 218, are laid out in narrow house lots with scattered small frame dwellings, a few larger buildings south of Lincoln Avenue in block 217, and a cement block making building beside the diagonal Lincoln Avenue. The Millstone River crosses the lower left corner. Much of the eastern half of the part is still vacant land. The 100 foot scale bar is printed at the bottom right.
notes: Washington Avenue here is today's Boesel Avenue; 3rd Street is Liberty Street and 4th Street is Cooper Street.
This part repeats 3rd Street (Liberty Street) from the upper part of the sheet; it is drawn below the heavy line because it lies east of the upper part on the ground.
